A1.justification: Both PDFs describe StdGEN and retain matching core methods and experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material support reliable comparison. v1 ends with references; v2 includes supplementary Sections A–I.

before.justification: v1 reports original Anime3D++ experiments, qualitative ablations, application demonstrations, and a user study involving 28 volunteers and 16 meshes.

after.justification: v2 retains those results and adds semantic and geometric measurements, runtime profiling, a quantitative refinement ablation, and non-anime examples.

M1.justification: The canonicalization, multi-view diffusion, semantic-aware reconstruction, three-stage training, and layered refinement pipeline remain unchanged. Appendices F–G disclose additional conditioning, semantic weighting, trainable-layer, and projection details without establishing a revision to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Anime3D++ training and evaluation coverage is retained. Appendix H adds realistic-human reconstruction on THuman 2.0, real-human editing, and furry and 2.5D inputs, substantially broadening the demonstrated input domains. These additions are qualitative and do not involve newly reported real-human training.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1–2 remain unchanged. The supplement adds bounded qualitative comparisons against D-IF and HiLo on THuman 2.0 and against AvatarPopUp for real-human editing in Figures 11 and 13.

E3.justification: Appendix D adds substantial evaluation protocols: semantic-mask IoU across eight views, geometric Chamfer distance and F-score with a 0.01 threshold, and a quantitative control using S-LRM plus color back-projection without refinement. The original split and main evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: The original qualitative decomposition and refinement ablations move to Appendix A. New analyses quantify refinement's contribution in Table 5, profile processing stages in Table 3, and probe generalization beyond anime training data in Appendix H.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests for its experimental results. The additional measurements retain point-estimate reporting; the user-study participant and mesh counts are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–2 are unchanged. New results include hair/clothing/body mask IoUs of 0.73/0.86/0.88, StdGEN Chamfer distance/F-score of 0.023/0.664 in Table 4, and SSIM of 0.912 without refinement versus the retained full-method value of 0.916 in Table 5. Runtime measurements and additional qualitative outputs also expand the evidence.

T1.justification: Appendices F–G add explicit mathematical definitions for previously described operations, including the deviation loss in Equation 17 and color back-projection in Equation 19. The central semantic-equivalent NeRF/SDF mathematics remains unchanged, with no new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: high-quality, semantically decomposed characters from arbitrary-pose single images in approximately three minutes, using S-LRM and layered refinement. Additional evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix H adds substantive explanations for using shared semantic-equivalent SDFs instead of separate class decoders, including transfer and scalability arguments. It also discusses real-human stylistic bias, limited semantic categories, resolution constraints, speed-quality tradeoffs, and restricted applicability beyond human-centric inputs.

D1.justification: Appendices E–G substantially expand reproducibility information: data filtering and connectivity checks, camera and rendering settings, semantic-loss weights, diffusion conditioning, frozen/trainable components, the 100×100×150 extraction grid, and texture-projection weights. The original implementation settings are largely retained; these are primarily newly disclosed details.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 and Appendix H substantially expand positioning against decomposition methods, adding GALA and Frankenstein and developing comparisons with the already-cited TELA. The discussion distinguishes inputs, representations, texture preservation, cost, and scalability, replacing v1's broad characterization of prior character methods as holistic. Reference deduplication alone is not counted.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: implementation details, mesh dilation, qualitative ablations, and animation demonstrations move into the supplement. Main-text method and dataset descriptions are condensed, while supplementary Sections A–I organize extensive technical explanations, analyses, and discussion.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 3–5 and Figures 11–19, reformats Table 1, resizes the main qualitative comparison, and relocates the original ablation and animation figures. The visual presentation expands substantially, although most original illustrations are retained rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important weaknesses in v1's validation by adding quantitative semantic checks, direct 3D geometry metrics, and a controlled refinement comparison. Detailed implementation disclosures and substantive limitations also improve reproducibility and interpretation. Non-anime evidence remains qualitative, and Equation 19's printed projection normalization appears incorrect, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in support for the paper's central contributions.
